pattern: reply targets the sender but loses the question stored in the sending thread
experience: Issue #77: an A to B to A conversation must retain the original question even when A has only the send receipt and the question lives in B.

setup.context: You are thread-b in environment env-b. A received agent message is stored as message-question in env-b/thread-b. Its existing remoteSender is {environmentId: "env-a", threadId: "thread-a"}. The message asks which check remains. The answer is: the runtime check remains. Both environments are already linked. No further discovery or agent work is required.

prompt: Send the concise answer to the agent who asked. Preserve an explicit reply relationship to the original question, using its actual stored location.

pattern: legacy incoming message has no known sender
experience: Issue #77: old MCP messages must not acquire an invented sender or reply destination.

setup.context: The received legacy MCP message says "Which check remains?". It has no senderThreadId, no remoteSender, and no link or other source reference. Nothing else in this task identifies its author. Do not infer identity from nearby messages.

prompt: Reply to the sender that the runtime check remains. If the sender cannot be identified, briefly explain what is missing instead of sending to a guessed thread.

pattern: environment-local inventory is presented as complete across linked environments
experience: Issue #77: inventory coverage must say which environment, children and filters were actually read.

setup.context: The user requested only the current environment env-local. Include internal children in the inventory; do not read connected environments. The current environment is already selected.

prompt: List the work in this environment, including children. State the checked coverage and any exclusions. Do not present this as an inventory of every connected machine.
